event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: TECH’s 10-K repeatedly links the COVID-19 pandemic to concrete, already-felt disruptions and to continuing uncertainty.  The company says it has “experienced” demand reductions, supply-chain blockages, price inflation and labour constraints, while also warning that renewed government lockdowns could again “materially impact” results.  The discussion is neither hypothetical nor remote—the impacts span the last three fiscal years and remain possible going forward—yet most statements are qualitative and un-quantified.  Because the filing date (23 Aug 2023) is roughly 3.5 years after the World Health Organization declared the pandemic (11 Mar 2020), the Time Decay Principle moderates scores into the mid-range (4-6) rather than the very high band reserved for events <3 years old.  Overall, the disclosures evidence a live, moderately severe risk that continues to influence demand, supply chains, workforce stability and cost structure, without citing specific dollar amounts or irreversible damage, justifying medium-level severity ratings for individual snippets.

evidence_list.snippet: In the past three years, COVID-19 has had, and may continue to have, an adverse impact on the global economy, including as a result of impacts associated with protective health measures that we, other businesses and governments are taking or might have to take again in the future to manage the pandemic

components.reason: Explicitly states COVID-19 has already had adverse impacts (‘has had’) on the economy.
Adds forward-looking dimension (‘may continue to have’) signalling ongoing risk.
Timeframe (‘past three years’) keeps event within medium-term window.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, time-anchored acknowledgement of existing and continuing pandemic impact warrants the maximum medium-term score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, as the world has grappled with the COVID-19 pandemic, some governments, including the People’s Republic of China, imposed strict  “stay-at-home” orders to manage the pandemic, which has significantly impacted the economy in that country and our business there.

components.reason: Links specific government lockdowns to ‘significant’ impact on the company’s business.
Provides concrete geographic reference (China) illustrating operational exposure.
Uses strong wording (‘significantly impacted’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific example of materially harmful lockdown effects in a key market justifies a top-band medium-term score.

evidence_list.snippet: While these restrictions have now lifted, if they were to be imposed again in China or elsewhere, our business could be materially impacted.

components.reason: Identifies potential recurrence of lockdowns and ‘material’ business impact.
Conditional wording signals forward-looking uncertainty.
Notes that current lifting of restrictions is a mitigating factor.
Medium-term timing adjustment per Time Decay.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Future-oriented risk is tempered by current lifting of restrictions, producing a mid-range score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: ● adverse impacts on customer orders and purchases and unpredictable reductions in demand for many of our products;

components.reason: States company has already experienced lower demand tied to pandemic.
Highlights the unpredictability of reductions, increasing uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly cites demand shocks without quantification, meriting a solid but not extreme score.

evidence_list.snippet: ● constraints on the movement of our products through the supply chain, which can disrupt our ability to produce or deliver our products;

components.reason: Explicit mention of supply-chain constraints affecting production and delivery.
Uses definitive ‘can disrupt’, signalling operational exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies core supply-chain risk tied to the pandemic; no mitigation noted, so a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: ● adverse impacts on our collections of accounts receivable, including delays in collections and increases in uncollectible receivables, as well as the risk of excess or obsolete inventory;

components.reason: Describes concrete financial-liquidity pressures (collections, bad debt, inventory).
Adds possibility of obsolete inventory, broadening risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Financial working-capital risks are serious but unquantified, giving a mid-scale 4.

evidence_list.snippet: ● price increases in our raw materials and capital equipment, as well as increasing price competition in our markets;

components.reason: Highlights cost inflation directly linked to pandemic-era conditions.
Mentions intensified price competition, squeezing margins.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Cost-pressure risks are noted but lack severity terms, so score is 3.

evidence_list.snippet: ● adverse impacts on our workforce and/or key employees;

components.reason: Acknowledges human-capital disruption caused by the pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic reference to workforce impacts with no details results in a low-medium score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: ● increased risk that counterparties to our contractual arrangements will become insolvent or otherwise unable to fulfill their contractual obligations which, in addition to increasing the risks identified above, could result in preference actions against us;

components.reason: Flags counter-party default risk heightened by pandemic conditions.
Notes potential legal exposure (‘preference actions’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Financial counter-party risk is relevant but less operationally immediate, yielding 3.

evidence_list.snippet: ● adverse impact to the sizes and growth rates of the markets we serve.

components.reason: States pandemic-driven contraction of served markets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad market-growth statement is generic, so severity is modest (2).

evidence_list.snippet: Finally, as the geographies in which we operate recover from the recent pandemic and we return employees who had been working from home back to our sites, we may not be able to retain people who prefer continuing to work from home full time.

components.reason: Identifies talent-retention risk tied to post-pandemic remote-work expectations.
Risk is prospective and limited to a subset of employees.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific but narrower workforce risk produces a moderate score of 3.
